heuristic_window_note: MVP temporal selection window of ±10 minutes around the anomaly timestamp; this is an evidence-selection heuristic, not a scientifically calibrated causal threshold.

anchor_non_discriminating.interpretation: The anchor event (loss of ground command contact) is consistent with multiple failure mechanisms and does not by itself discriminate among them.

anchor_supporting_persistent_fault.interpretation: Extended command unresponsiveness is consistent with a persistent command-system fault, but does not establish whether the underlying mechanism was hardware, software, latchup, or another failure mode.

anchor_supporting_unresolved.interpretation: The anchor event documents a persistent anomaly whose causal mechanism is not established by the available environmental or spacecraft data.

env_ep8_window.interpretation: GOES-13 EP8 1 MeV electron flux measured within the ±10-minute heuristic investigation window establishes that an energetic-particle environment existed contemporaneous with the anomaly. This is a precondition observation — it documents what the environment was, not that a specific mechanism occurred. GOES-13 is a proxy measurement; direct in-situ flux at the spacecraft bus is unavailable.

env_mag_window.interpretation: GOES-13 MAG B_GSM measurements within the ±10-minute heuristic investigation window document geomagnetic field conditions contemporaneous with the anomaly. B_GSM is the local field at GOES-13 orbit, not at the target spacecraft body. Geomagnetic field magnitude does not directly support or exclude an SEU or latchup mechanism — that determination requires particle flux data.

hypotheses.label: Single-event electronic upset / latchup
hypotheses.description: A high-energy particle traversed the command-receiver integrated circuit, causing a single-event upset (SEU) or latchup that rendered the uplink receiver unresponsive.

limitations.description: GOES-13 EP8 measurements are a proxy. Direct in-situ particle flux at the spacecraft bus is unavailable.
No onboard SEU detection or latchup protection status data is available in this dataset.

hypotheses.label: Command receiver / command-processing fault
hypotheses.description: A fault internal to the command receiver or command-processing chain produced a persistent loss of command uplink capability independent of the external environment.

limitations.description: Autonomous recovery provides evidence against an irreversible catastrophic failure, but does not distinguish among recoverable hardware, software, or power-state mechanisms.
No spacecraft command-subsystem telemetry or onboard fault logs are present in this dataset.

hypotheses.label: Insufficient evidence for causal attribution
hypotheses.description: The available evidence is insufficient to establish a causal mechanism for this command anomaly. This is a legitimate outcome of the investigation, not a failure to analyse.

limitations.description: Causal attribution is not established by the available evidence. Multiple hypotheses remain plausible and cannot be discriminated without additional data.
Key discriminating data — spacecraft command-subsystem telemetry, onboard fault logs, and direct in-situ particle measurements — are absent from this dataset.
